title: SAD Demands CBI Probe Into Attack on Sukhbir Badal, Alleges Conspiracy Against Moderate Leadership
excerpt: The Shiromani Akali Dal seeks a high court-monitored investigation, while PM Modi's call to Harsimrat Kaur Badal draws cross-party attention to the security situation in Punjab.
body:
• Shiromani Akali Dal demands CBI investigation and a high court-monitored probe into the attack on party president Sukhbir Singh Badal, alleging a "deep conspiracy to eliminate moderate leadership"
  • SAD leader Bikram Singh Majithia accused unnamed forces of targeting the moderate Sikh leadership, calling it an assault on Punjab's political stability
  • PM Modi called Sukhbir Badal's wife Harsimrat Kaur Badal after the attack; she described herself as "deeply touched" by the gesture

The Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) has demanded a CBI investigation and a high court-monitored probe into the attack on its president Sukhbir Singh Badal, describing the incident as part of a "deep conspiracy to eliminate the moderate leadership" of the party and the Sikh community.

SAD leader Bikram Singh Majithia, who is Badal's brother-in-law, said the attack was not an isolated act of violence but a coordinated effort to destabilise moderate Akali leadership in Punjab. He called for an impartial investigation by a central agency, arguing that the Punjab Police probe cannot be trusted to be unbiased.

SAD Alleges Conspiracy Against Moderate Sikh Leadership

Addressing the media, Majithia said the attack exposed the vulnerability of moderate political leadership in Punjab to extremist elements. "This is a deep conspiracy to eliminate the moderate leadership of SAD," he said, demanding that the investigation be handed over to the CBI and monitored by the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

"This is a deep conspiracy to eliminate the moderate leadership of SAD. We demand a CBI investigation and a high court-monitored probe."

— Bikram Singh Majithia, SAD leader

The SAD core committee convened an emergency meeting and unanimously decided to approach the Punjab Governor seeking an impartial investigation. The party has rejected the Punjab Police's handling of the case, alleging political interference and inadequate security arrangements.

According to reports from ThePrint and Telegraph India, the party plans to submit evidence to the Governor and demand that the investigation examine broader conspiracy angles, including potential involvement of individuals beyond the immediate attacker.

PM Modi's Call and Political Reactions

Prime Minister Narendra Modi personally called Harsimrat Kaur Badal, the former Union Minister and wife of Sukhbir Badal, to enquire about the situation. In a statement, Harsimrat said she was "deeply touched" by the Prime Minister's gesture.

The attack has drawn condemnation across political lines. Leaders from the BJP, Congress, and other parties have expressed concern over the security situation, with several demanding accountability from the state government.

The Hindu reported that the attack exposes the Akali Dal's vulnerability to radical fringe elements, noting that the party's moderate stance — which has historically sought to balance religious conservatism with democratic politics — has made its leadership a target for extremists who reject the mainstream political process.

Implications for the Sikh Community

The attack carries broader significance for the global Sikh community. The Shiromani Akali Dal, one of the oldest political parties in India, has long positioned itself as the mainstream political voice of the Sikh community. Any threat to its leadership resonates deeply with Sikh diaspora communities in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Australia.

The incident also raises questions about the security environment in Punjab, particularly around religious sites. SAD has drawn parallels to past security failures, including the 2022 murder of singer Sidhu Moose Wala, to argue that the state government has failed to protect its critics.

The investigation's outcome and the government's response will be closely watched by diaspora organisations that maintain strong ties with Punjab's political and religious institutions.
